You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer plugin):
- file: include/hybrid/reg_names.h:2
- category: stale-doc
- title: Header comment claims the register-name tables are used by vsim's gdbstub handback client - that consumer was removed with the QEMU2 leg
- detail: reg_names.h lines 1-3 say the tables are 'Used by the QEMU TCG plugin (C) at drain time and by vsim's gdbstub handback client (C++) at restore time.' CLAUDE.md states the QEMU2 handback leg was removed entirely. I grepped for hybrid_gpr_names/hybrid_fpr_names/reg_names across /home/nick/work/andesim (plugin + driver/) and /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim: the only consumers are qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c lines 7/180/181 and the ABI's own compile checks (include/tests/abi_compile_check.c/.cpp). No gdbstub handback client exists in the vsim repo's src/. Note this file lives in the include/ submodule (andesim_abi repo), so the fix is a submodule commit + pointer bump; the C++ extern-C guards can stay since the compile check builds it as C++.
- claimed safety: Comment-only change; no token outside comments is touched, so the compiled plugin and the ABI compile checks are unaffected.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. - iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.

in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a

1	// Shared GDB register-name tables. Used by the QEMU TCG plugin (C) at
2	// drain time and by vsim's gdbstub handback client (C++) at restore
3	// time. The strings are the gdb wire contract for QEMU's RISC-V
4	// gdbstub - any reordering or renaming must be done in lock-step here.
5	
6	#ifndef HYBRID_REG_NAMES_H
7	#define HYBRID_REG_NAMES_H
8	
9	#ifdef __cplusplus
10	extern "C" {
11	#endif
12	
13	// Index = x register index. Matches the names in QEMU's
14	// gdb-xml/riscv-64bit-cpu.xml (the wire contract for qemu_plugin_register
15	// lookup). NB: x8 is "fp", NOT "s0" -- QEMU's gdbstub uses the
16	// frame-pointer alias. Looking it up as "s0" yields a NULL handle and
17	// silently zeros gpr[8] in the drained state.
18	static const char *const hybrid_gpr_names[32] = {
19	    "zero", "ra",  "sp",  "gp",  "tp",  "t0", "t1", "t2",
20	    "fp",   "s1",  "a0",  "a1",  "a2",  "a3", "a4", "a5",
21	    "a6",   "a7",  "s2",  "s3",  "s4",  "s5", "s6", "s7",
22	    "s8",   "s9",  "s10", "s11", "t3",  "t4", "t5", "t6",
23	};
24	
25	// Index = f register index. From riscv-64bit-fpu.xml.
26	static const char *const hybrid_fpr_names[32] = {
27	    "ft0", "ft1", "ft2",  "ft3",  "ft4", "ft5", "ft6", "ft7",
28	    "fs0", "fs1", "fa0",  "fa1",  "fa2", "fa3", "fa4", "fa5",
29	    "fa6", "fa7", "fs2",  "fs3",  "fs4", "fs5", "fs6", "fs7",
30	    "fs8", "fs9", "fs10", "fs11", "ft8", "ft9", "ft10","ft11",
31	};
32	
33	#ifdef __cplusplus
34	}  // extern "C"
35	#endif
36	
37	#endif  // HYBRID_REG_NAMES_H
38
